title: Between two sal trees
hook: at Kusinara he lies down on his right side; the trees blossom out of season (DN 16)
carry: rest is part of the path

segments.voice: Yesterday: Cunda's meal, and a dying teacher who made sure the cook was never blamed. Your line: no one is to blame.

Visit a Buddhist temple and you may find him lying down. A huge golden figure, stretched out on his right side, head resting on one hand, eyes half closed, calm as a Sunday afternoon. It's easy to take it for a nap. It's something else. It's today. After Cunda's meal, sick and weak, the Buddha walks on toward a small town called Kusinara. He stops to rest along the way. He crosses a river. And at a grove of sal trees outside the town, he says to Ananda: I'm tired. I want to lie down.
screen: `THE RECLINING BUDDHA.` → `NOT A NAP.` → `I'M TIRED. I WANT TO LIE DOWN.`

segments.voice: Please, Ananda, he says, prepare a couch for me between these two sal trees, with my head to the north. Ananda does. The Buddha lies down on his right side in what's called the lion's posture, one foot resting on the other, mindful and clearly aware. That's the pose in the great statues. Not sleep. Awake, at rest, at the end. Then, the text says, the twin sal trees burst into flower out of season, and blossoms drift down onto his body. Flowers and sandalwood powder fall from the sky, and music plays from somewhere above, all in his honor. Here's the turn. The Buddha tells Ananda, in effect: this is not how the one who found the way is truly honored. Not with flowers. Whoever lives by the teaching, practicing it well in small matters and great, honors him. Even with the trees in bloom, he points away from the show and back to the practice. And the simplest part is quietly radical. He lay down. The great teacher, who had walked from town to town all his teaching life, said he was tired, and rested. The path wasn't only effort; rest was part of it, especially here. In the same hours, the text tells of Ananda going off alone, leaning on a doorpost, and weeping. My teacher is passing away, he says, the one who was so kind to me. The Buddha sends for him, comforts him, and praises him in front of everyone. Tomorrow, one more visitor arrives at the grove.
screen: `HEAD TO THE NORTH, ON HIS RIGHT SIDE.` · `SAL TREES BLOOM OUT OF SEASON.` · `HONOR ME BY PRACTICE.` · `ANANDA WEEPS BY THE DOOR.` · then, large: `REST IS PART OF THE PATH.`

segments.voice: If you can, lie down now, on your right side if that's comfortable, or on your back; if you can't, lean back and let your body be heavy. Feel what holds you up, and feel your breath slow down by itself. There's nothing to do and nowhere to get to: rest, awake, and let this be practice too.
Kusinara. The small town near which the Buddha, tired after Cunda's meal, asked Ananda to prepare a couch between two sal trees and lay down to rest.
Your line: rest is part of the path. Even the Buddha said: I'm tired. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Reclining Buddha images, showing him on his right side between the sal trees at Kusinara, are found in temples across Asia, and pilgrims visit Kushinagar in India, where a large reclining image marks the place.

original.note: Pali: the sal tree (Shorea robusta), under which, tradition says, the Buddha was also born.

trapdoor: what you thought: a statue of the Buddha lying down to sleep.
what it means: his last hours at Kusinara, awake, at rest, pointing past the flowers to the practice.
what a scholar hears: DN 16, 5.1–5.14: sihaseyya, the lion's posture; the twin sal trees; honor by practice (dhammanudhammapatipanna).

chat.says: Why do some Buddha statues show him lying down?
options: They show him at the end, awake and at rest between two sal trees.
They show him taking a nap after a long day of teaching.
They show him meditating at the moment of his awakening.
chat.meaning: Tired after Cunda's meal, he lay on his right side between two sal trees, mindful and aware. Not sleep: awake, at rest, at the end.

Kusinara.meaning: the small town where the Buddha lay down at the end

sal.meaning: a tall flowering tree of India

lion's posture.meaning: lying on the right side, one foot resting on the other

Cunda.meaning: the metalworker who served the last meal

Ananda.meaning: the Buddha's cousin and longtime attendant

notes: Reclining Buddha at Wat Pho, Bangkok, is about 46 m long, longer than a basketball court (about 28 m). Confirm.
Tradition that the Buddha was born under a sal tree (Lumbini): the birth tree is often called sal or asoka depending on source. Confirm the note.
Ananda weeping at the doorpost and the Buddha's praise of him: DN 16, 5.13–5.16. Confirm.
Forty-five years of teaching: traditional count; confirm.
